drivingQuestion: What is taught by the double yod in ״וייצר ה׳ אלהים את האדם״?
outcomeNote: Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda's two-inclinations reading is defeated by the animal case; the double yod is re-expounded either as R' Shimon ben Pazi's 'woe from my Creator, woe from my inclination' or as R' Yirmeya ben Elazar's du partzufin, and both alternatives are left standing side by side.

segments.he: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״וַיִּיצֶר ה׳ אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם״ בִּשְׁנֵי יוֹדִין? — שְׁנֵי יְצָרִים בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, אֶחָד יֵצֶר טוֹב וְאֶחָד יֵצֶר רָע.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda interpreted homiletically: What is the meaning of that which is written: “Then the Lord God formed [vayyitzer] man”» (Genesis 2:7), «with a double yod?» This double yod alludes to that fact that «the Holy One, Blessed be He, created two inclinations; one a good inclination and one an evil inclination.»

segments.he: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בְּהֵמָה דְּלָא כְּתִיב בַּהּ ״וַיִּיצֶר״ לֵית לַהּ יִצְרָא? וְהָא קָא חֲזֵינַן דְּמַזְּקָא וְנָשְׁכָא וּבָעֲטָא! אֶלָּא כִּדְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי ״אוֹי לִי מִיּוֹצְרִי וְאוֹי לִי מִיִּצְרִי״.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak strongly objects to this: If that is so,» does «an animal, with regard to whom vayyitzer is not written» with a double yod, «not have an inclination? Don’t we see that it causes damage and bites and kicks? Rather,» interpret the double yod homiletically, «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, as Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said:» This alludes to the difficulty of human life; «woe unto me from my Creator [yotzri] and woe unto me from my inclination [yitzri].» If one opts to follow either his Creator or his inclination, woe unto him from the other.

segments.he: אִי נָמֵי כִּדְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: דּוּ פַּרְצוּפִין בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אָחוֹר וָקֶדֶם צַרְתָּנִי״.
segments.en: «Alternatively,» this duplication in the language of creation can be explained «in accordance with» the statement of «Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar, as Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, created two faces [du partzufin] on Adam the first» man; he was created both male and female in a single body, «as it is stated: “You have formed me [tzartani] behind and before”» (Psalms 139:5); tzartani is derived from the word tzura [face]. God formed two faces on a single creation, back and front.

moves.cueHe: דרש רב נחמן בר רב חסדא
moves.summary: expounds the double yod of vayyitzer as the creation of two inclinations, good and evil
moves.about: brings the verse of man's formation, whose vayyitzer is written with two yods, as the material of his exposition

moves.cueHe: מתקיף לה רב נחמן בר יצחק
moves.summary: objects that on this reading animals, lacking the doubled vayyitzer, would have no inclination, yet they damage, bite and kick
moves.about: whether the doubled yod can be what signals the two inclinations, given that an animal, of whom vayyitzer is not written at all, visibly has an inclination — it damages, bites and kicks

moves.summary: substitutes R' Shimon ben Pazi's reading — woe from my Creator and woe from my inclination — as the sense of the double yod
moves.about: adduces R' Shimon ben Pazi's dictum as the correct sense of the doubled yod in place of the reading he has just attacked

moves.cueHe: אי נמי כדרבי ירמיה בן אלעזר
moves.summary: offers a second alternative: the doubled formation language teaches R' Yirmeya ben Elazar's du partzufin
moves.about: adduces R' Yirmeya ben Elazar's du partzufin teaching as a second way of accounting for the doubled language of formation

moves.summary: proves du partzufin from ״אחור וקדם צרתני״, tzartani read as a term of tzura
moves.about: brings the verse 'You have formed me behind and before' as the prooftext for du partzufin; the citation is internal to the quoted dictum and belongs to its speaker

edges.about: brings the verse of man's formation, whose vayyitzer is written with two yods, as the material of his exposition

edges.cueHe: דרש רב נחמן בר רב חסדא: מאי דכתיב
edges.about: the doubled yod of vayyitzer teaches that the Holy One created two inclinations in man, a good one and an evil one

edges.cueHe: מתקיף לה רב נחמן בר יצחק: אלא מעתה
edges.about: whether the doubled yod can be what signals the two inclinations, given that an animal, of whom vayyitzer is not written at all, visibly has an inclination — it damages, bites and kicks

edges.cueHe: אלא כדרבי שמעון בן פזי, דאמר רבי שמעון בן פזי
edges.about: adduces R' Shimon ben Pazi's dictum as the correct sense of the doubled yod in place of the reading he has just attacked
re-expounds the doubled yod of vayyitzer as the tension between yotzri (my Creator) and yitzri (my inclination), not as two inclinations

edges.cueHe: אי נמי כדרבי ירמיה בן אלעזר, דאמר רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר
edges.about: adduces R' Yirmeya ben Elazar's du partzufin teaching as a second way of accounting for the doubled language of formation

edges.cueHe: אי נמי כדרבי ירמיה בן אלעזר
edges.about: the doubled language of formation in vayyitzer is alternatively explained as Adam's creation with two faces rather than as two inclinations
edges.proposedPredicate: interpret.offers_alternative_interpretation — «אי נמי» — files a second, equally admissible reading of the same words alongside one already given, without rejecting it; interprets/interprets_verse name the act of expounding but not the alternation, rejects_proposal_of would falsely make the first reading fail, and disputes_with would falsely make two parties hold rival views

edges.about: brings the verse 'You have formed me behind and before' as the prooftext for du partzufin; the citation is internal to the quoted dictum and belongs to its speaker

edges.cueHe: דו פרצופין ברא הקדוש ברוך הוא באדם הראשון, שנאמר
edges.about: reads tzartani as a term of tzura (face) so that 'behind and before' says Adam was formed with two faces in one body
